title: Balanced quotient tower at the geometric point
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}D.k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $B$ be the completed integral coefficient sheaf on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $C,J$ be arbitrary cochain complexes of $B$-module sheaves, with sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and signed total [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Then the tower of separately reduced total tensors [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] is isomorphic to the identity scalar-extension quotient tower of their ordinary signed total tensor [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. The forward isomorphism sends $(a\otimes x)\otimes(b\otimes y)$ in each bidegree and each quotient to $ab\otimes(x\otimes y)$, including after sheafification, for all local sections $a,b,x,y$. No flatness, constructibility or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Lemmas 3.4.11--3.4.12; agent-written chain-coordinate argument in completion normalization steps 1--2

proof.text: Apply the existing tensor reduction tower comparison. Multiplication identifies the identity scalar reduction with ordinary reduction. The inverse balancing rule multiplies the quotient scalars; its inverse inserts one in the first tensor factor. The balanced relations prove the two inverse equations. Sheafification gives the corresponding sheaf maps; the direct sum over bidegrees gives complex maps commuting with both signed differential summands. Multiplication commutes with every quotient transition, so the level maps assemble to the required strict tower isomorphism.
